nodes.label: Retention Policy Gate on Segment Storage
nodes.rationale: record.enabled alone keeps nothing: continuous recording is off by default, so cached segments are only moved to disk when they match a configured continuous/motion/alerts/detections retention policy. This conserves storage by default at the cost of being the single most common reason recordings appear empty.

nodes.label: Recording RAM Cache and Maintainer
nodes.rationale: Segments are first written to a RAM cache (/tmp/cache) and moved to disk by frigate.record.maintainer. Frigate discards the oldest cached segments rather than exhausting memory and crashing, trading lost footage for stability.

nodes.label: PIPELINE_ERROR_DECODE Playback Failure
nodes.rationale: Frigate copies the record stream to disk without re-encoding, so the browser must decode exactly what the camera produced. Chromium's media pipeline is stricter than VLC/ffmpeg, so a file valid to ffprobe can still fail in a browser; this is outside Frigate's control by design.

nodes.label: Incompatible Audio Codec in MP4 Container
nodes.rationale: G.711 variants (pcm_alaw/pcm_mulaw) cannot be muxed into MP4, so ffmpeg silently fails to write the segment even while live view works; the fix is transcoding audio to AAC or dropping it via an ffmpeg preset.

nodes.label: Smart Codec / H.264+ Timestamp Corruption
nodes.rationale: Smart/"+" codec modes change encoding parameters mid-stream and drop keyframes, corrupting timestamps so segments split roughly every second and fill the cache 10x faster than expected.

nodes.label: Hourly Preview Clip Assembly
nodes.source_location: My timeline previews are black after restarting Frigate
nodes.rationale: Preview frames are cached in tmpfs and only assembled into a clip at the top of each hour, so recreating the container mid-hour discards the partial hour. Expected behavior, unrelated to shm_size; a soft UI restart preserves the cache.
